recipe: Turn brief into a requirement matrix with IDs, priority, source, verification method and explicit unknowns; separate delivery specs from aesthetic preferences.
Write a single sentence visual promise; select one dominant motif, two supporting motifs and an explicit reject list; compare three hero frames at thumbnail size.
Vary storytelling mechanism (object transformation, observational scene, spatial metaphor), not merely palette; score feasibility and audience resonance independently.
Identify viewing device, prior knowledge, accessibility needs and decision point; validate the first five seconds with an unbriefed reviewer.
Use a 1-primary/2-secondary message map; assign screen-time and visual salience separately; strip any item competing with the core claim.
Build a timecoded shot table with cut duration, focal subject, motion direction, light, palette and sound cues; distinguish measured evidence from interpretation.
Specify palette in tagged color space, two type families at most unless justified, texture scale, edge treatment, motion curves and reference exclusions; compare hero and supporting shots.
Run one identical 2-second hero test per candidate style; evaluate readability, rendering cost and asset feasibility before committing.
Define emotional beats on a 0–5 intensity curve; map each turning point to a visible action and one sound or intentional silence.
Record locks as machine-readable fields (camera matrix, text policy, immutable ROI, language, duration); validate before and after render.
Break work into dependency graph with asset-ready, animatic, lookdev, picture-lock and delivery gates; isolate optional experiments from critical path.
Benchmark a representative frame or short clip for candidate engines; compare capabilities, licenses, RAM, failure modes and interoperability before selecting.
Allocate integer frames per shot using rational FPS and transition overlap; reconcile final total, then estimate cost using measured p50/p95 frame time.
Create asset register with dimensions, usable crop, rights, dependencies and fallback; test hero asset at final scale before designing around it.
Use severity × likelihood matrix; require early probe for any high-impact risk (e.g. rig, font, adapter, color); define measurable exit condition.
Keep constraints and content identical across variants; change one major creative grammar per variant; score on same rubric and archive rejected options.
Record accepted or rejected preferences with scope, provenance, timestamp and opt-out; current brief always wins; do not retain raw sensitive source assets by default.
Build tokens for brand colors, fonts, logo padding, forbidden treatments and mandatory copy; pixel-compare protected master assets rather than redrawing them.
Assign stable series asset IDs, reusable environments, character continuity states, episode-specific beats and an approval migration policy.
Deliver project manifest, version hashes, reproducible render command, open risks, locked items and next steps; verify on a clean directory if possible.
Write a beat outline before dialogue; ensure each scene changes visible state; budget action, reading time and intentional silence in frames.
Use subject + goal + obstacle or promise + stakes in one sentence; verify the logline predicts the film rather than describing its genre.
Place turning points using available runtime rather than fixed percentages; remove any act that repeats exposition; check payoff setup.
Limit cast/locations for short format; establish a clear visual question early and answer it in a distinct final image.
Create a silent storyboard test; replace explanatory text with actions, reactions or object state where permitted; verify causal chain.
Draft in breath-length phrases; read at realistic pace, mark pauses and emphasized words; use actual recording length before picture lock.
Give each speaker an objective and distinctive rhythm; read alternating lines aloud and remove spoken explanations already visible.
Test opening without audio at thumbnail scale; require one unmistakable subject or action, without clickbait or an unsupported promise.
Seed one visual motif or question early, then return with altered meaning; avoid repeating the entire summary in an end card.
Map setup, reveal, reaction and transition to integer-frame intervals; ground each beat in an observable event and track overlap.
Specify shot ID, in/out frame, lens/size, movement, blocking, light direction, audio cue, dependencies and protected regions.
Draw or render the first, decisive and final pose per shot; add eyelines, axis, camera arrows and frame timing outside the deliverable.
Build low-cost timeline with scratch VO and motion placeholders; review once muted and once audio-only before detailed production.
Use floor plan with camera axis and eyeline vectors; test contact poses and entrances; preserve screen direction except intentional axis reset.
Track identity, wardrobe, positions, prop ownership, light vector and character state at every cut; flag mismatches before render.
Use claim IDs and source locators with publication date; distinguish quotes, paraphrases and unverified assertions; avoid fabricated archival footage.
Build master and necessary cutaway coverage with matched action handles; verify edit has alternatives without bloating shot count.
Localize meaning and natural rhythm; log terms that must remain unchanged; re-time visuals and captions from actual localized audio.
Assign chapter question, resolution, starting time and transition; preview navigation and avoid repetitive introductions.
Keep CTA actionable and truthful; test dwell time against copy length; ensure final crop and language variant retain offer terms.
Set subject-height fraction, eye line and crop bounds; compare wide/medium/close for information needs; preserve action handles.

Overlay thirds only for composition review; place subject deliberately, then check balance, silhouettes and platform crops without guides.
Plot vanishing directions and subject eye path; remove lines that pull attention out of frame; test in low-detail grayscale.
Reserve normalized empty rectangle for visual breathing room or text; test against per-platform overlays and moving foreground objects.
Pin camera world transform, projection, focal length, shift and crop; compare matrices at every frame if available; do not fake motion with animated crop.
Animate position along explicit path with continuous velocity; choose ramp relative to shot length; test foreground parallax and clipping at extremes.
Use target-relative offset and filtered look-at with fixed up vector; inspect occlusion, acceleration and collision through full path.
Orbit explicit pivot using sin/cos angle, constant radius or designed easing; use stable up vector and inspect axis flip near poles.
Animate height and horizontal travel separately; maintain sightline and horizon intent; check lens clearance and endpoint reveal.
Match angular direction and exposure across cut; tune short shutter blur around rotation, not whole shot; inspect peak for unintended white flash.
Use seeded low-frequency positional/rotational drift with bounded amplitudes; avoid independent random noise each frame; review at real speed.
Keep distance × tan(vertical FOV/2) constant for fixed subject height; derive new focal from sensor height; test projected size drift at start/mid/end (suggest ≤2%).

Use physically plausible subject scale, working distance, shallow DOF and broad highlights; compare legibility of detail before adding blur.
Use world-scale altitude, smooth banking and planned route; check horizon, terrain clearance and scale cues over whole path.
Place camera near character eye position with consistent handedness and eyeline; limit artificial roll unless narratively motivated.

Choose geometry families by story role; compare silhouette-only frames and limit conflicting stylistic primitives.
Measure hierarchy through grayscale, blur and thumbnail tests; suppress competing contrast or motion around the focal point.

Design clear negative space, type scale and image cropping; use restrained editorial transitions and inspect actual reading holds.

Set believable small-world scale, lens angle and depth cues; use selective focus only if readable details survive.
